<p dir="auto">
This framework provides an easy method to compute embeddings for accessing, using, and training state-of-the-art embedding and reranker models. It can be used to compute embeddings using Sentence Transformer models (
<a href="https://sbert.net/docs/quickstart.html#sentence-transformer" rel="nofollow">quickstart</a>
), to calculate similarity scores using Cross-Encoder (a.k.a. reranker) models (
<a href="https://sbert.net/docs/quickstart.html#cross-encoder" rel="nofollow">quickstart</a>
), to generate sparse embeddings using Sparse Encoder models (
<a href="https://sbert.net/docs/quickstart.html#sparse-encoder" rel="nofollow">quickstart</a>
) or to compute token-level embeddings for ColBERT-style late-interaction retrieval using Multi-Vector Encoder models (
<a href="https://sbert.net/docs/quickstart.html#multi-vector-encoder" rel="nofollow">quickstart</a>
). This unlocks a wide range of applications, including 
<a href="https://sbert.net/examples/applications/semantic-search/README.html" rel="nofollow">semantic search</a>
, 
<a href="https://sbert.net/docs/sentence_transformer/usage/semantic_textual_similarity.html" rel="nofollow">semantic textual similarity</a>
, and 
<a href="https://sbert.net/examples/applications/paraphrase-mining/README.html" rel="nofollow">paraphrase mining</a>
.
</p>
<p dir="auto">
A wide selection of over 
<a href="https://huggingface.co/models?library=sentence-transformers" rel="nofollow">15,000 pre-trained Sentence Transformers models</a>
 are available for immediate use on 🤗 Hugging Face, including many of the state-of-the-art models from the 
<a href="https://huggingface.co/spaces/mteb/leaderboard" rel="nofollow">Massive Text Embeddings Benchmark (MTEB) leaderboard</a>
. Additionally, it is easy to train or finetune your own 
<a href="https://sbert.net/docs/sentence_transformer/training_overview.html" rel="nofollow">embedding models</a>
, 
<a href="https://sbert.net/docs/cross_encoder/training_overview.html" rel="nofollow">reranker models</a>
, 
<a href="https://sbert.net/docs/sparse_encoder/training_overview.html" rel="nofollow">sparse encoder models</a>
 or 
<a href="https://sbert.net/docs/multi_vector_encoder/training_overview.html" rel="nofollow">multi-vector encoder models</a>
 using Sentence Transformers, enabling you to create custom models for your specific use cases.
</p>

For the 
<strong>full documentation</strong>
, see

<a href="https://www.sbert.net" rel="nofollow">www.SBERT.net</a>
</strong>
.
</p>

from sentence_transformers import SparseEncoder

# 1. Load a pretrained SparseEncoder model
model = SparseEncoder("naver/splade-cocondenser-ensembledistil")

# The sentences to encode
sentences = [
    "The weather is lovely today.",
    "It's so sunny outside!",
    "He drove to the stadium.",
]

# 2. Calculate sparse embeddings by calling model.encode()
embeddings = model.encode(sentences)
print(embeddings.shape)
# [3, 30522] - sparse representation with vocabulary size dimensions

# 3. Calculate the embedding similarities
similarities = model.similarity(embeddings, embeddings)
print(similarities)

#         [    0.098,     0.019,    29.553]])

# 4. Check sparsity stats

print(f"Sparsity: {stats['sparsity_ratio']:.2%}")

<p dir="auto">This framework allows you to fine-tune your own sentence embedding methods, so that you get task-specific sentence embeddings. You have various options to choose from in order to get perfect sentence embeddings for your specific task.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>
Embedding Models

<ul dir="auto">
<li>
<a href="https://www.sbert.net/docs/sentence_transformer/training_overview.html" rel="nofollow">Sentence Transformer > Training Overview</a>
</li>
<li>
<a href="https://www.sbert.net/docs/sentence_transformer/training/examples.html" rel="nofollow">Sentence Transformer > Training Examples</a>
 or 
<a href="https://github.com/huggingface/sentence-transformers/tree/main/examples/sentence_transformer/training">training examples on GitHub</a>
.
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
Reranker Models

<ul dir="auto">
<li>
<a href="https://www.sbert.net/docs/cross_encoder/training_overview.html" rel="nofollow">Cross Encoder > Training Overview</a>
</li>

 or 
<a href="https://github.com/huggingface/sentence-transformers/tree/main/examples/cross_encoder/training">training examples on GitHub</a>
.
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
Sparse Embedding Models

<ul dir="auto">
<li>
<a href="https://www.sbert.net/docs/sparse_encoder/training_overview.html" rel="nofollow">Sparse Encoder > Training Overview</a>
</li>
<li>

.
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
Multi-Vector (Late Interaction) Models

<ul dir="auto">
<li>
<a href="https://www.sbert.net/docs/multi_vector_encoder/training_overview.html" rel="nofollow">Multi-Vector Encoder > Training Overview</a>
</li>
<li>
<a href="https://github.com/huggingface/sentence-transformers/tree/main/examples/multi_vector_encoder/training">Training examples on GitHub</a>
.
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Some highlights across the different types of training are:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>
Support of various transformer networks including BERT, RoBERTa, XLM-R, DistilBERT, Electra, BART, ...
</li>
<li>
Multilingual and multi-task learning
</li>
<li>
Evaluation during training to find optimal model
</li>
<li>
<a href="https://www.sbert.net/docs/package_reference/sentence_transformer/losses.html" rel="nofollow">20+ loss functions</a>
 for embedding models, 
<a href="https://www.sbert.net/docs/package_reference/cross_encoder/losses.html" rel="nofollow">10+ loss functions</a>
 for reranker models and 
<a href="https://www.sbert.net/docs/package_reference/sparse_encoder/losses.html" rel="nofollow">10+ loss functions</a>
 for sparse embedding models, allowing you to tune models specifically for semantic search, paraphrase mining, semantic similarity comparison, clustering, triplet loss, contrastive loss, etc.
</li>
</ul>

<p dir="auto">The following Hugging Face blog posts complement this documentation with narrative walkthroughs and full training examples:</p>
<p dir="auto">

<ul dir="auto">
